obtained.how: agency copy: DFO's own PDF of CSAS Research Document 2016/002 (vi + 550 p.), as captured by the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine on 5 Aug 2016 and openly downloadable. DFO's current address for the report redirects to a CSAS page that needs JavaScript (not run by the script)

bibliography.note: the report's own form: 'Katopodis, C. and Gervais, R. 2016. Fish swimming performance database and analyses. DFO Can. Sci. Advis. Sec. Res. Doc. 2016/002. vi + 550 p.' The entry's URL now redirects to a JavaScript-only CSAS page; the Wayback capture of the PDF is a stable copy

claims.claim: fish sprint at 7–19 body lengths a second (3-s bursts on the DFO fatigue curves)
claims.conditions: dimensionless group fatigue curves U* = K·t*^b with U* = U/√(gl), t* = t·√(g/l): mean regression lines through forced and volitional swim tests of many species, fitted over 3 s to 30 min; temperature not a variable
claims.note: U/l = K·(g/l)^((1+b)/2)·t^b. Table 3a: Catfish & Sunfish K 2.176, b −0.202; Salmon & Walleye 4.004, −0.250; Pike (derived) 3.811, −0.329. At t = 3 s the slowest of the project's fish is smallmouth at 30 cm (C&S) 7.01 BL/s and the fastest blacknose dace at 7 cm (S&W) 19.42 BL/s. The range is the project's computation at its chosen lengths, not a range the report states

claims.claim: Catfish & Sunfish group: pumpkinseed (15 cm) 9 / 2.5, brown bullhead (25 cm) 7.5 / 2.1, smallmouth (30 cm) 7 / 1.9, redbreast (18 cm) 8.6 / 2.4 BL/s at 3 s / 30 min
claims.location: p. 25 (PDF p. 25), group membership; p. 26 (PDF p. 26), Table 3a; p. 530 (PDF p. 530), Table A2a (Centrarchidae and Ictaluridae in the group)
claims.quote: Smallmouth Bass and Largemouth Bass were placed in the Catfish and Sunfish Group
claims.conditions: the group's own comment: 'Limited data on burst range' (Table 3a), so its 3-s speeds are extrapolated; its 95 % prediction band spans K 1.424–3.326 (Table 3b)
claims.note: recomputed: 9.24 / 2.54, 7.54 / 2.07, 7.01 / 1.92, 8.59 / 2.36. Ictaluridae data are channel and blue catfish; brown bullhead and pumpkinseed themselves are not in the database

claims.claim: Salmon & Walleye group: yellow perch and white perch (20 cm) 13 / 2.6, white sucker (40 cm) 10 / 2.0, fallfish (25 cm) 12 / 2.4, blacknose dace (7 cm) 19.4 / 3.9 BL/s at 3 s / 30 min
claims.location: p. 25 (PDF p. 25); p. 26 (PDF p. 26), Table 3a; pp. 531–533 (PDF pp. 531–533), Table A2a (Cypriniformes — Catostomidae, Cyprinidae incl. Rhinichthys and Semotilus — Moronidae and Percidae under the Salmon and Walleye Group)
claims.quote: Percidae (Walleye, White Perch and Yellow Perch) were placed in the Salmon and Walleye Group
claims.note: recomputed: 13.10 / 2.65, 10.10 / 2.04, 12.05 / 2.43, 19.42 / 3.92. (The report's sentence lists White Perch under Percidae by a slip; Table A2a puts Morone americana under Moronidae, in the same group.) The notes call the cyprinids' assignment an inference, but Table A2a places Cyprinidae in this group explicitly

claims.claim: chain pickerel (45 cm) 7.5 / 0.9 BL/s at 3 s / 30 min on the DFO pike curve
claims.location: pp. 25–26 (PDF pp. 25–26); Table 3a; p. 531 (PDF p. 531), Table A2a
claims.quote: Pike Group (Derived) - curve derived by assuming burst performance similar
claims.note: recomputed 7.47 / 0.91. The pike curve's burst end is ASSUMED (from the Salmon & Walleye and Eel groups): the pike data (northern pike, tiger muskellunge) are all in the low prolonged range, and there are no chain pickerel data — so the pickerel's 3-s speed is an assumption twice over

claims.claim: banded killifish (7 cm) 12.5 / 3.4 BL/s on the catfish–sunfish curve
claims.location: p. 495 (PDF p. 495), Figure F7-a: Cyprinodontidae among the Unclassified Species
claims.quote: Processed data for the Unclassified Species
claims.note: recomputed 12.52 / 3.44. The report puts killifish and topminnows (Cyprinodontidae: Fundulus notatus, F. zebrinus) in NO group; using the catfish–sunfish curve is the project's choice (the code says so), not the report's

notes: Definitions (p. 7): burst < 20 s, prolonged 20 s–30 min ending in fatigue, sustained = held indefinitely; so the code's 'sustain' (the 30-min speed) is the slow end of the prolonged range, as its comment says. Species-level curves exist for some of the lakes' fish and differ from the group means: white sucker's own regression (Table A2a: K 7.9895, b −0.3776, n 287, burst and prolonged) gives ~14.3 BL/s at 3 s and ~1.3 at 30 min for a 40-cm fish, against the group's 10.1 / 2.0. The alewife's speeds in the code (15 / 3.0, marked [inf]) are not from this report; its Herring Group curve (K 10.119, b −0.402; Alosa including alewife) would give ~23 BL/s at 3 s and ~1.8 at 30 min at 14 cm, if a sourced value is wanted.
